message.content: Copernicus founded his heliocentric theory during the Renaissance, when printing, humanist learning, and religious tension transformed European intellectual life. Politically, monarchs were centralizing power, the papacy remained influential, and early Reformation disputes were beginning to weaken Catholic unity. In Poland, relative stability under the elective monarchy and the Diet created a comparatively safer environment for scholars to pursue natural philosophy. Yet any challenge to accepted cosmology had to be presented cautiously, almost cactiform, wrapped in mathematical language to avoid appearing as direct doctrinal rebellion.
